items.line: PopBase, a news aggregator account, posts that Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer and that the Vatican confirms it. A story on this page sets out what the Vatican and the Associated Press reported.
Netflix posts a video, saying it shows how Narnia was created in Narnia: The Magician's Nephew, a film by Greta Gerwig, in theaters February 12.
A user posts a video with the caption: remembering the day they downloaded Letterboxd and marked every movie they had ever watched as watched.

Unusual Whales posts that the United Nations adopted a global pandemic preparedness declaration by 153 to 3, per UN News, with the United States, Israel and Argentina voting against. Not checked here.

A user asks Grok which state Katie Zacharia, named in the post as Trump's new press secretary, passed the bar exam in, saying she has repeatedly called herself a lawyer. Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI, which is named in the post. Not checked here.
Kamala Harris says people are tired of choosing between gas and groceries because of what she calls Donald Trump's war in Iran, and that they are ready to stop him.
Yoxics says RaKai had to call 911 over trouble breathing while trying to set a record for most T-shirts worn at once. A video is attached. Not checked here.
A user posts a video captioned "Windows 7 on PS5".

In Spanish, a user lists what they say are details of a discarded version of RE9 called "Resident Evil Apocalypse", with Jill, Leon, Ada and Sheva as leads. The post does not say where the details come from. Not checked here.

Sternenko says Starlink terminal operation in Ukraine was restricted overnight, with connections dropping above 160 km/h, and that SpaceX likely acted at the Trump administration's request. Not checked here. Another account replies that Starlink and Starshield are different services.
Radosław Sikorski asks Elon Musk whether he is playing politics with his products again, and tells him European customers are watching. The post quotes another post that is not recorded here.
BRICS Info posts that India's High Commissioner says Canada will need 15,000,000 new immigrants over the next decade to meet job demand. Not checked here.
Walter Bloomberg (DeItaone), a markets news account, reports US September CPI inflation at 3.7% against 3.6% expected, with core at 2.6% against 2.5%, and gasoline up 9.1%. Not checked here.
Tesla says its Roadster event will stream live this Thursday at 7:55pm CST.
Joshua Barzon posts a map of every hurricane to hit the United States over 173 years and says Virginia, Maryland and Delaware seem to have a "magical hurricane force field". Not checked here.
In Portuguese, UpdateCharts posts a video saying Lula announced "Pé de Meia Universitário" together with students. Not checked here.

OpenAI says it found a hidden recording device in one of its offices, that an employee planted it, and that the FBI made an arrest. It says it has no sign of access to model weights, source code or customer data, and that the employee was terminated. Not checked here.

A user says a Grok Bot saved them more than $1,000 by filing a complex tax return with overseas reporting, and that they only reviewed and submitted it. Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI, which is named in the post. Not checked here.

A user says they made a Grok Bot that uses Suno, Midjourney and Opus to make music videos, and posts a 20-second teaser it made. Grok is made by xAI, the company behind the model that gathers this page's posts; Opus is made by Anthropic, the company behind the model that writes it. Not checked here.
Nature Unedited posts a video captioned "Before and after the dog park". The video is not described in the capture.
A user says Shaquille O'Neal posted a video on TikTok and that people in the comments are going wild. The video is not described in the capture.
PopBase posts that today is National I Love You Day.
RivalsAssembled posts a video and says a new legendary Mr. Fantastic skin has been revealed.

Fox News Politics says security camera footage reviewed by The New York Times disproves a rumor about where Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico was during nine days in early October, and that his campaign said he had the flu. Not checked here.

Volodymyr Zelensky says a Russian ballistic missile attack hit Kyiv's CHPP-4 energy plant and damaged a residential building, and that Ukraine got no early warning from partners. He says Russia is preparing more launches. Not checked here.
Remarks, a news account, posts that Canadian Prime Minister Carney says he plans to increase immigration into Canada. Not checked here.
Nick Sortor says President Trump announced full pardons for three Alaskans charged over fixing engines, and quotes Trump saying they faced 10 years in jail. Not checked here.
BBC World reports that Saudi Arabia has overturned a death sentence given to a man over a Facebook comment.

Adam Schefter reports that a jury returned a mixed verdict in the civil assault and battery trial against Tyreek Hill, finding him liable on two battery counts and not liable on the eight other claims by his estranged wife. Not checked here.

Eric Daugherty, a political commentator, posts that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America over 475 apparent sanctions violations, and quotes Bessent saying the biggest institutions are not above the law. Not checked here.
NASA announces an update on Oct. 23 on its plans to return American astronauts to the Moon by 2028, with details on the upcoming Artemis III mission to test systems needed for future Moon landings.

Osint613 reports that Israel’s government approved nearly NIS 1 billion in an emergency phone vote to buy 12 Apache helicopters, and that the US State Department has already approved a possible sale of AH-64E Apaches. Not checked here.
Arsenal posts a photo captioned "The class of 26/27".
The account of the Mayor of New York City posts a greeting for the Hindu festival of Navaratri, naming Garba dancing, Sindur Khela and Golu displays in homes.

HormuzLetter says Ukraine struck an oil depot in Valuyki, Belgorod Oblast, and launched over 500 drones into Russia overnight, the first strike on energy sites since a US-announced energy ceasefire. Not checked here.

SpaceX posts a video and photos of Starship Ship 40, which it says was the first Starship to return to its launch site. It says the ship now stands in a Megabay at Starbase and will give data on a flown heatshield, engines and avionics.

Paul Graham, a founder of the startup accelerator Y Combinator, posts that a Tesla Model 3 with FSD drove him and his wife to the gym with no hands on the controls, and calls it mind-blowing. His account of one drive; not checked here.

Fox News reports that a Georgia police officer shot and killed a miniature donkey named HeeHaw while officers searched a farm for a missing child. It says the officer claims the donkey charged, the owner says it was only approaching people, and the officer is on administrative leave.

CBS Sports Golazo posts a video captioned "Kate really went there with Micah." A fan account in also says it shows Kate Abdo introducing Micah Richards on CBS Sports with a joke about medals. The video itself is not described in the capture.
K-charts account kchartsmaster reports that muuo:23, a five-member K-pop group made with generative AI by Creation Zipup, pre-debuted with a single called NEVERTHELESS.
In Arabic, an account posts two photos captioned "Prince Hussein and Princess Rajwa in their last appearance." The photos are not described in the capture and the post is not checked here.
Fabrizio Romano reports that Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr has been suspended for four La Liga games, which would include El Clásico. Not checked here.

The Baltimore Banner posts a video and says Republican Rep. Andy Harris incorrectly told a reporter they were breaking the law while recording him after a debate with Democratic challenger Dan Schwartz. Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm posts a new trailer for a Muhammad Ali biopic series, executive produced by Michael B. Jordan, which it says arrives on Prime Video on November 4.

Ari Meirov, citing @sportsrapport, says Joe Buck and Troy Aikman argued before Monday night's Rams-Bills game over their ESPN contract situations. ProFootballTalk repeats the report. Not checked here.
